function: Joint AP scheduling (high level, large timescale) and joint AP active precoding plus RIS phase shifts (low level, small timescale) maximizing sum spectral efficiency (pp. 1-3).
system: Distributed MIMO: S=4 APs with M=4 antennas, L=2 passive reflecting RISs with N=64 elements, K=4 single-antenna users, B=2 scheduled APs; band not stated (pp. 1, 4).
method: Hierarchical deep reinforcement learning: discrete SAC for AP scheduling, multi-agent SAC for AP precoding and RIS phase shifts; centralized training, distributed execution (pp. 2-3).
data_channel: Custom simulated Rician channels (K1=K2=6 dB, K3=2 dB), distance path loss, random direct-link blockage; no separate test data stated; no standard model or dataset (pp. 1, 4).
test_conditions: Trained at Pb,max=10 dBm and tested directly at other transmit powers (Fig. 4); retrained for each number of RIS elements and scheduled APs (Figs. 5-6) (p. 5).
baselines: Non-learned: BFS-AO, two-timescale (BFS plus AO), random precoding, no RIS. Learned: HPPO, Random-SAC (random AP scheduling, trained low level) (p. 4).
metrics: System sum spectral efficiency (bit/s/Hz) versus maximum transmit power, number of RIS elements, and scheduled APs; training convergence; complexity orders (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Big-O orders: high-level O((KMS+C(S,B))I+I^2), low-level O((KMB+N)I+(L+B)I^2); two-timescale O(C(S,B)) and O(I1(I2B^2M^2K^2+I3L^2N^2)) (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 1: "Utilizing the Rician fading channel model, the channels are modeled as"; p. 4: "The path loss exponents for the AP-RIS, RIS-user and AP-user links are set as". Custom Rician simulator with its own path loss; no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing dataset or measurement is named.
q2_support: p. 5: "The HDRL algorithm trained at Pb,max = 10 dBm is directly tested in other scenarios" is a transmit-power (SNR) sweep of the same setup; p. 5: "retrain the HDRL algorithm to adapt to different scenarios" for N and B, so retraining for each condition. No new scenario, band, dataset or site is tested.
q3_support: p. 4: "integrates the HDRL framework with the PPO algorithm": HPPO is the proposed hierarchical framework with PPO in place of SAC (a variant) and Random-SAC is an ablation. BFS-AO and two-timescale (non-learned) are compared on sum SE (p. 5, Figs. 4-6), but no earlier published learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 5: "Given the number of neurons I in the hidden layer, the computational complexity" of the high-level and low-level controllers is given as O((KMS+C(S,B))I+I^2) and O((KMB+N)I+(L+B)I^2), against O(C(S,B)) and O(I1(I2B^2M^2K^2+I3L^2N^2)) for the two-timescale method.
q5_support: p. 4: "In this setup, two RISs are located at" a self-defined geometry with simulated channels; the paper gives no code or data link, DOI, or public dataset.
notes: PDF title (p. 1) is 'Joint AP Scheduling and Precoding in RIS-Aided Distributed MIMO Networks: A Hierarchical DRL Framework' and the DOI printed on p. 1 matches. Area 3: the learned controllers set the AP active precoding and the RIS phase shifts (p. 3) and AP scheduling is learned jointly with them, so above_phy does not apply. Borderline marks for the reviewer: q2 treats the transmit-power sweep of Fig. 4 as an SNR sweep (it would be 1 if the reviewer counts it as a new condition); q3 treats HPPO as a variant of the proposed framework (it would be 1 if the reviewer counts PPO as a standard learning algorithm applied to the same problem). Frequency band not stated; no code or data release found.
